text:
The board is the feature herddash is measured by: a notification center with one box per agent showing status, owning account and time waiting, sorted longest-waiting first; read-only, no terminal, no chat, no pane control. The recorder engine (subscribe, persist transitions, attribute, read-only API, event stream) is what makes the board trustworthy and feeds future surfaces. Corrects ADR-0001's consequence that the board is secondary; to be recorded as ADR-0003.

Why: The operator's daily value is glancing at the board in another window all day; a PRD that calls it secondary would produce epics that treat it as secondary, the success metric (noticing a waiting agent sooner than the toast) is a board metric, and the differentiator the operator believes in is restraint, a notification center rather than a browser client, which can only be defended if the board is the product being restrained.

Epoch rule (spine AD-3, Story 1.6): on the first snapshot after every reconnect, keep the server epoch only if at least one tracked pane is present with the same non-empty terminal_id; otherwise increment it, removing every tracked Agent under the old epoch. Within a kept epoch, a pane whose pane id survives but whose terminal_id changed is a new Agent, never joined. A pane-id match alone never keeps an epoch. The epoch lives in memory until milestone 2 persists it with the pane-to-terminal_id map (hazard 3 open).

Why: Story 1.3 found herdr names no server instance; a new one shows as a new terminal_id per pane (observed ids look time-derived, e.g. term_65df2e06a79ca1 → term_65df2e18d44a41, not counters), and a fresh server reissues pane ids from w1:p1. Agents do not survive a non-handoff herdr restart (restored panes run fresh shells), so incrementing on a new instance is truthful. Effect of server.live_handoff on terminal_id is untested.

Story 1.7 resync design (spec-1-7): resync is a named engine operation triggered by any status-stream health signal, a rejected/failed status subscribe, or a snapshot showing a tracked Agent without a subscription. One resync runs at a time, a trigger during one causes exactly one more, and resyncs start at least resyncMinInterval (default 5 s) apart. Each resync is announced via Sink.Resynced(cause) as it begins, resubscribes unsubscribed panes, and ends when a snapshot read started after those subscribes settled has been applied. apply() subscribes only newly tracked panes, which bounds the rejection loop deferred from Story 1.5. A reconcile timer requests a snapshot every reconcileInterval (default 60 s). Lifecycle-stream signals keep Story 1.6's reconnect, whose Reconnected report is the marker.

Why: AD-11 requires a single resync guard and minimum interval in the engine, and FR-7 requires every gap to be announced. Funnelling the per-pane recovery paths through one guarded operation serialises a lost-events condition that drops many pane connections, and makes the persistent-rejection loop cost one subscribe per interval. The lifecycle stream already has a reconnect that resubscribes, snapshots and replaces state.

text: macOS omits the environment from kern.procargs2 for Apple-signed binaries (e.g. /bin/sleep) when the caller is not root: only exec path and argv come back. herddash's procenv treats a buffer with no environment entries as ErrNoEnvironment, so the Profile is `unresolved` rather than the rule's absent case. Claude Code's binary is signed by Anthropic (Identifier com.anthropic.claude-code, TeamIdentifier Q6L2SF6YDW, checked 2026-10-19), so its environment is readable. Tests that need a readable child environment on darwin must spawn a non-Apple binary, e.g. the test binary re-executed (TestHelperSleep in cmd/herddash/serve_test.go).

Story 2.1 store (spec-2-1): store.Open(path) works in this order. It refuses a database parent directory that is not owner-only (any group or other permission, or another owner), creating it 0700 if missing; this also covers --database outside data_dir. It takes an exclusive non-blocking flock on <db>.lock (ErrLocked names the path), refuses a PRAGMA user_version above the binary's highest migration (ErrSchemaNewer) before writing, turns on WAL, then applies embedded internal/store/migrations/NNNN_*.sql in one transaction that also sets user_version. Migration 0001 creates transitions (id = recording order; host/server/epoch/pane_id; agent_program, profile; previous/new_status; state_change_seq NULL; herdr_version; provenance CHECK; possibly_spurious 0/1; observed_at ms; import_key UNIQUE NULL) and resync_markers (host/server/epoch/observed_at/reason). serve opens the store at cfg.Database() and exits 1 if that fails. Pins: modernc.org/sqlite v1.60.1 and libc v1.77.1.

Why: AD-9, AD-10 and ADR-0005 fix the lock, the migrations and the record's fields. Any later change to the transitions table needs an ADR, so the full column set lands in 0001. The stricter owner-only parent rule follows FR-17 and Story 1.2's deferred item. Opening the store in serve now makes a second Daemon fail at once.

Story 2.2 recording (spec-2-2): the engine writes every Transition through store.Append when it observes it, including an Agent's first sight as a Transition with no previous Status (snapshot provenance from apply, live from a status event). It writes a daemon_start resync marker at Run start. The epoch and pane→terminal_id map persist in a mutable server_state table (migration 0002), upserted after a snapshot changes them. At start the engine loads them and runs Story 1.6's epoch rule on the first snapshot. History reads order by observed_at then id (the binding spine rule); the epic AC's "herdr's order" wording is superseded by the Story 1.3 finding. A failed write is logged, never fatal.

Why: ADR-0005 and AD-4 make the record append-only, but the epoch is engine state, not the record. Without persisting it, a Daemon restart restarts at epoch 1 and splices a new herdr instance's Agents onto old history (AD-3 hazard 3). Recording first sight makes the record hold every Agent's current Status (FR-7 consequence 2). Story 2.4 owns deciding how the fold treats a first-sight row whose Status equals the last stored one.

Story 2.3 resync markers (spec-2-3): marker reasons are daemon_start, connect (first ready connection of a run), reconnect, the Story 1.7 resync causes verbatim (events_lost, error, rejected, closed, undecodable) and reconcile. Detail holds herdr's error code for events_lost/error/rejected, and "epoch kept"/"epoch incremented" for connect/reconnect when the epoch rule ran. Connect, reconnect and resync markers are written before the rows of the snapshot that ends the gap, after the state save and with the epoch in force. A reconcile marker is written after the rows, and only when that reconcile read changed something (a snapshot Transition, a first sight or a removal).

Why: FR-7: a gap must be a recorded fact. Marking before the rows reads as "gap, then reconciled state". A reconcile is known to have disagreed only after apply. Story 2.4 Waiting Time (spec-2-4): core.ClassOf maps blocked→needs_you, done→finished, idle→finished if the Agent was ever working (else working), working→working, unknown/none→unknown. core.Fold over an Agent's ordered Transitions gives Status, Class, Since (the ObservedAt of the Transition where the current class began; done→idle keeps it), SinceProvenance and EverWorking. Add(t) extends a result incrementally. WaitingTime is exact only when SinceProvenance is live, else a lower bound now−Since. The engine keeps a fold per pane. At first sight with a store, it reads History(key): if the last stored Status equals the one seen, it writes no row and keeps the fold (exact survives a Daemon restart); if they differ, it records a Transition whose previous Status is the stored one. serve prints class= and waiting= (≥ for a lower bound).

Why: AD-12 requires one fold computing Waiting Time from the record. Story 2.2's unconditional first-sight rows would reset every Waiting Time on a Daemon restart (FR-8). A real herdr restart increments the epoch (Story 1.6), so "no Transition across a herdr restart" holds for kept-epoch reconnects.

Story 2.5 Retention (spec-2-5): store.Sweep(ctx, cutoff, present) is the only DELETE in non-test code (enforced by TestOnlyDelete). In one transaction it deletes transitions older than the cutoff, except, for each present Agent (same host/server/epoch/pane), rows at or after its fold's Since (all of them when Since is 0) and its newest working row; and it deletes resync_markers older than the cutoff. The engine runs it on a run-wide timer (default 1 h; the first sweep at the first ready connection), skipping while not connected and ready or while a resync is running or scheduled. The present set includes tracked panes still awaiting Profile resolution, with Since 0. RetentionDays 0 disables it.

Why: AD-4 and FR-9 fix what may be deleted. Including pending first sights keeps the history that their history-seeded first sight (Story 2.4) is about to read, so the first sweep cannot reset a Waiting Time. Markers are swept by age too, so the database stays bounded (a persistently rejected pane writes a marker every 5 s).

text: Store calls in herddash must not run under a context that shutdown cancels. When a transaction's context is cancelled, database/sql rolls it back in a background goroutine, and DB.Close does not wait for that connection. So right after Store.Close returns, SQLite's lock can still be held, and the next store.Open gets SQLITE_BUSY. This was seen once on Linux CI in TestServeTwice (PR #30) and did not reproduce on macOS. The engine therefore passes context.WithoutCancel(runCtx) to Sweep and History. The cause is inferred from database/sql's semantics, not proven.

Story 2.6 import (spec-2-6): `herddash import-plugin-log <file> --herdr-0.9.2-since <date>` parses the agent-webhook hook.log. It handles two forms (`posted <status> for <pane> -> <code>`, and `would have sent {json}` with an optional profile), with local-time stamps. Each entry becomes a backfill Transition under epoch 0, with NULL previous Status, state_change_seq and herdr version. The import_key is a SHA-256 of host, server and the raw line, plus the occurrence index. `done` entries before local midnight of the given date are flagged possibly spurious. On a Host that never ran 0.9.2+ (this machine's server is 0.8.2), pass a date after the last entry. Entries older than Retention are skipped. Rows are written by store.AppendBackfill: the same INSERT as Append, in one transaction, skipping existing import keys. Spine AD-13 is amended to say so.

Why: FR-9a and AD-13. Host and Server are in the key so a mis-keyed first import can be corrected by re-running with the right flags. A batch transaction makes the import all-or-nothing and fast. It shares the single INSERT statement, so the rows cannot differ in shape from the engine's.

3.2:
- After each inbox message that changed something visible, the engine publishes an immutable engine.View: a run id (random per Daemon start), Seq (+1 per publication, starting at 1), the sorted AgentViews, the workspace headers and a core.ConnectionTruth.

- Engine.View() is lock-free (atomic.Pointer). Engine.Subscribe(buffer) gives a bounded channel that is closed on overflow, and at shutdown after a final connected:false publication.

3.3:
- httpapi.New(View func) serves only GET/HEAD /api/state.
- The Host check runs first: localhost, 127.0.0.1 or [::1] with any port is allowed, anything else gets 403 host_not_allowed.
- Other methods get 405 with Allow: GET, HEAD; unknown paths get 404. The JSON error shape is used throughout.
- Every response carries no-store and nosniff, and never a CORS header.
- serve listens on cfg.Bind() before the engine starts and shuts down gracefully. Config now accepts port 0, which tests use.

Why: AD-2, AD-6, AD-7 and ADR-0007: readers never lock engine state, and the HTTP surface is read-only, loopback-only, and built from the published view with no herdr call per request.

Stories 3.4 and 3.5 (stream and history).

3.4: GET /events is SSE.
- Opening: subscribe (buffer 64), then take View(), then send `retry: 2000` and `event: state` (id = Seq, data = the /api/state body). After that, only publications with a higher Seq are sent.
- Event names are httpapi constants (agent, removed, transition, resync, connection), mapped explicitly from the engine's change kinds.
- A transition event carries the key, wireTransition (import_key is not sent; observed_at is in ms) and the new AgentView.
- Per-write deadline 10 s; keepalive every 15 s; Last-Event-ID is ignored.
- Handler.CloseStreams is registered with RegisterOnShutdown. After it runs, or once the engine has stopped, /events answers 503 unavailable.

3.5: GET /api/agents/{host}/{server}/{epoch}/{pane}/history.
- Segments are percent-decoded one at a time; the epoch must be digits.
- It reads through an injected History function (serve passes store.History) and returns {key, transitions: [wireTransition]} in record order.
- No rows gives 404; a store error gives 500 internal.

Why: AD-7 and FR-13: subscribing before taking the snapshot means no gap; explicit names keep the public contract stable; and 503 with a retry hint prevents EventSource reconnect storms. AD-6 and FR-14: history is read-only and comes from the record alone.
